name: UT-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Kennedy running with large financial advantage ($386K on hand vs. $1K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at just 4%
Democratic challenger raised only $54K with no outside support
model.rationale: The district's R+17 partisan lean, Kennedy's overwhelming fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Republican win at 94% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or expert ratings suggest any competitive threat to the incumbent.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or independent expenditure targeting Kennedy could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Utah's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of roughly 17 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mike Kennedy is running for reelection and holds a decisive financial advantage, with about $387,000 on hand compared to roughly $1,100 for Democratic challenger Jonny Larsen, who has raised only about $54,000. No independent or outside spending has been reported on either side.

Prediction markets give Kennedy about a 94% chance of winning, and no general-election polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive. A Libertarian and an independent candidate are also on the ballot but pose little threat. The forecast expects Kennedy to win comfortably by a margin in the mid-to-high teens, consistent with the district's underlying lean.
